title: Producer-consumer pattern — ReentrantLock+Conditions, wait/notifyAll, BlockingQueue

s1_definition.profdef: The producer-consumer pattern decouples data PRODUCTION from CONSUMPTION using a shared buffer. Producers add items; consumers remove them. When the buffer is FULL, producers WAIT. When EMPTY, consumers WAIT. Three implementations: (1) **BlockingQueue** (simplest, production-ready) — `put()` blocks when full, `take()` blocks when empty. Zero synchronization code needed. (2) **ReentrantLock + two Conditions** — `notFull.await()` for producers, `notEmpty.await()` for consumers. Targeted wake-ups. (3) **synchronized + wait/notifyAll** — classic, one wait-set (less efficient). All three: condition MUST be checked in a `while` loop (spurious wake-ups + stolen conditions).
s1_definition.analogy: **Producers** = market feed systems dropping trade orders onto a counter. **Consumers** = settlement tellers picking up orders and processing them. **Bounded buffer** = the counter has limited space (e.g., 100 slots). Counter full → feed systems WAIT. Counter empty → tellers WAIT. **BlockingQueue** = a professional queue management system — handles all waiting automatically. **Lock+Conditions** = separate waiting rooms for feed systems (notFull) and tellers (notEmpty). **wait/notifyAll** = one shared waiting room — shout wakes everyone, most go back to sleep.
s1_definition.oneliner: Producer-consumer: BlockingQueue (simplest, best for production). Lock+2 Conditions (targeted wake-ups). wait/notifyAll (classic, wasteful wake-ups). ALWAYS while loop for wait condition.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** The producer-consumer pattern decouples data PRODUCTION from CONSUMPTION using a shared buffer. Producers add items; consumers remove them. When the buffer is FULL, producers WAIT. When EMPTY, consumers WAIT. Three implementations: (1) **BlockingQueue** (simplest, production-ready) — `put()` blocks when full, `take()` blocks when empty. Zero synchronization code needed. (2) **ReentrantLock + two Conditions** — `notFull.await()` for producers, `notEmpty.await()` for consumers. Targeted wake-ups. (3) **synchronized + wait/notifyAll** — classic, one wait-set (less efficient). All three: condition MUST be checked in a `while` loop (spurious wake-ups + stolen conditions).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** **Producers** = market feed systems dropping trade orders onto a counter. **Consumers** = settlement tellers picking up orders and processing them. **Bounded buffer** = the counter has limited space (e.g., 100 slots). Counter full → feed systems WAIT. Counter empty → tellers WAIT. **BlockingQueue** = a professional queue management system — handles all waiting automatically. **Lock+Conditions** = separate waiting rooms for feed systems (notFull) and tellers (notEmpty). **wait/notifyAll** = one shared waiting room — shout wakes everyone, most go back to sleep.

**One line to remember:** Producer-consumer: BlockingQueue (simplest, best for production). Lock+2 Conditions (targeted wake-ups). wait/notifyAll (classic, wasteful wake-ups). ALWAYS while loop for wait condition.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The trade matching engine needed a bounded buffer between market feed (producer) and settlement (consumer).** Requirements: back-pressure when settlement falls behind (bounded buffer), zero lost trades, maximum throughput. First attempt: wait/notifyAll — worked but notifyAll woke 200 threads per trade (CPU spikes). Second attempt: Lock+2 Conditions — targeted wake-ups, much better. Final: `LinkedBlockingQueue(10000)` — zero custom code, two internal locks for concurrent put+take, proven implementation. Throughput: 50K trades/sec.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Buffer capacity = 5. 5 producers add trades. Buffer fills to 5 → producers call `notFull.await()` → WAIT.

**Step 2.** 3 consumers call `take()` → poll trade → call `notFull.signal()` → ONE producer wakes → adds trade → buffer at 5 again.

**Step 3.** Cycle continues: consumers empty slots → producers fill them. Buffer never exceeds 5 (back-pressure). All 50 trades eventually consumed.

**Step 4.** With BlockingQueue: same behavior, zero custom code. `put()` blocks when full, `take()` blocks when empty. Two internal locks allow concurrent put+take.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ PRODUCER-CONSUMER PATTERN ═══

  Producers ──put──→ [Bounded Buffer (capacity N)] ──take──→ Consumers
                     Full → producers WAIT
                     Empty → consumers WAIT

  ═══ THREE IMPLEMENTATIONS ═══

  1. BlockingQueue (BEST):
     queue.put(item)  → auto-blocks when full
     queue.take()     → auto-blocks when empty
     ZERO custom sync code!

  2. Lock + 2 Conditions (targeted):
     notFull.await()   → producers wait
     notEmpty.await()  → consumers wait
     notEmpty.signal() → wakes ONE consumer only!
     notFull.signal()  → wakes ONE producer only!

  3. wait/notifyAll (classic, wasteful):
     buffer.wait()      → both wait on SAME set
     buffer.notifyAll() → wakes ALL (99% go back to sleep!)
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — BoundedBuffer with Lock + 2 Conditions ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  BoundedBuffer<T>                     │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────── │
  │  - queue: Queue<T>                   │
  │  - capacity: int                     │
  │  - lock: ReentrantLock               │
  │  - notFull: Condition                │  producers wait here
  │  - notEmpty: Condition               │  consumers wait here
  │  ─────────────────────────────────── │
  │  + put(T item): void                 │
  │    lock → while(full) notFull.await()│
  │    queue.add(item)                    │
  │    notEmpty.signal() → wake consumer │
  │    unlock                             │
  │  + take(): T                         │
  │    lock → while(empty) notEmpty.await()│
  │    item = queue.poll()                │
  │    notFull.signal() → wake producer  │
  │    unlock → return item              │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  vs LinkedBlockingQueue (JDK built-in):
  - TWO separate locks (putLock + takeLock)
  - Concurrent put and take!
  - Same bounded semantics
  - Production-proven, zero bugs
  - ALWAYS prefer this over custom implementation!
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The producer-consumer pattern uses a bounded buffer to decouple production from consumption. Three implementations: (1) `BlockingQueue` (best for production) — `put()` auto-blocks when full, `take()` auto-blocks when empty, zero custom synchronization. `LinkedBlockingQueue` uses two internal locks for concurrent put+take. (2) `ReentrantLock` + two `Condition`s (`notFull`, `notEmpty`) — targeted wake-ups, each signal wakes only the right type of thread. (3) `synchronized` + `wait()`/`notifyAll()` — classic but wasteful, notifyAll wakes ALL threads when only one needs to act.

All three require the wait condition in a `while` loop (not `if`) — spurious wake-ups and stolen conditions. In production: always use `BlockingQueue`. Custom BoundedBuffer with Lock+Conditions is an interview exercise to demonstrate understanding. In banking: trade matching engine → `LinkedBlockingQueue(10000)` between market feed producers and settlement consumers. Back-pressure: when settlement falls behind, producers naturally slow down (buffer full → put blocks). 50K trades/sec throughput with zero lost trades.
